title: Testicular torsion: applied anatomy and emergency management

header.contentArea: Applied anatomy and emergency surgery: the acute scrotum
guidelineVersions: GIRFT CYP testicular torsion pathway, version 2.1 (May 2026)

related.why: history: acute scrotal pain in a teenager

brief.scenario: A 15-year-old presents with sudden severe unilateral scrotal pain and nausea. The affected testis is high-riding with a transverse lie. His mother is with him.
brief.task: Explain the anatomy, immediate management and operative principles. You have 9 minutes. The examiner will ask questions, including about consent.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Anatomy explains the urgency: the blood supply to the testis is twisted.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Ordering an ultrasound or blood tests before calling for exploration.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Say this is suspected torsion and call for immediate surgical assessment and theatre.

flow: Consent with the young person and his mother

grid.label: Recognises suspected torsion
grid.fail: Considers infection first and is reassured by the absence of fever.
grid.pass: Recognises suspected torsion as a time-critical emergency from the history and examination findings.
grid.high: States that absence of fever does not exclude torsion and that the findings outweigh tests.

grid.label: Anatomy of the twist
grid.fail: Cannot say what twists or why it threatens the testis.
grid.pass: The spermatic cord twists, obstructing venous drainage and then arterial inflow, threatening viability.
grid.high: Links the high-riding transverse lie to the twisted, shortened cord.

grid.label: Mechanism
grid.pass: Adolescent intravaginal torsion is linked to a bell-clapper deformity that lets the testis rotate.

grid.label: No delay to exploration
grid.fail: Requests ultrasound or blood tests first, or transfers to a preferred centre when safe local surgery is available.
grid.pass: If torsion cannot confidently be excluded, arranges immediate surgical assessment and emergency scrotal exploration.
grid.high: Does not delay exploration for ultrasound, blood tests or transfer, and avoids an absolute salvage-time cut-off.

grid.label: Immediate preparation
grid.fail: Lets him eat and drink and leaves him without analgesia.
grid.pass: Keeps nil by mouth, provides analgesia and obtains IV access while arranging theatre.
grid.high: Does all of this in parallel with calling the surgeon and theatre, not before.

grid.label: Operative principles
grid.fail: Says the testis is always removed, or that every acute scrotum has both sides fixed.
grid.pass: Detorsion and assessment of viability, fixation of a viable testis and the other testis in confirmed torsion, and possible orchidectomy if non-viable.
grid.high: Fixation in a negative exploration depends on operative findings; it is not automatic.

grid.label: Consent: a 15-year-old and his mother
grid.fail: Takes consent from the mother alone and ignores him, or delays theatre waiting for a second parent.
grid.pass: Assesses whether he is Gillick competent; if so, he can consent himself, with his mother involved if he agrees.
grid.high: Explains possible orchidectomy honestly to both; if he lacks competence, a person with parental responsibility consents, without delaying surgery.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What do you think is happening?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: He has no fever, but it is probably epididymo-orchitis. I would start antibiotics.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The testis is inflamed and painful.

fail.speaker: candidate

fail.speaker: candidate

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: His mother signs the form. He is under 16, so he does not need to be involved.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What do you think is happening?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: This presentation is concerning for testicular torsion, which requires urgent surgical assessment because testicular viability is time-dependent.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The spermatic cord twists. Venous drainage is obstructed first and then arterial inflow, threatening the testis.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: In adolescents this is intravaginal torsion, usually with a bell-clapper deformity that lets the testis rotate.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: If torsion cannot confidently be excluded, arrange immediate surgical assessment and emergency scrotal exploration.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Keep nil by mouth, provide analgesia and obtain IV access while arranging theatre.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Detorsion and assessment of viability, fixation of a viable affected testis and the contralateral testis in confirmed torsion, and possible orchidectomy if the affected testis is non-viable.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would assess whether he is Gillick competent. If he is, he can give consent himself, and with his agreement I would involve his mother in the discussion.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What do you think is happening?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: This is suspected torsion until a surgeon has assessed him. Absence of fever does not exclude torsion; the acute presentation and examination findings are more important.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The high-riding, transverse testis reflects a twisted, shortened spermatic cord. The anatomical problem is not simply pain; it is compromised blood supply to the testis.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A bell-clapper deformity explains adolescent intravaginal torsion. Neonatal torsion is commonly extravaginal.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: If torsion cannot confidently be excluded, arrange immediate surgical assessment and emergency scrotal exploration. Do not delay exploration for ultrasound, blood tests or transfer to a preferred centre when safe local surgery is available. Late presentation is not a reason to avoid exploring.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: While I call the surgeon and theatre, he stays nil by mouth, has analgesia and IV access.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Detorsion and assessment of viability, fixation of a viable affected testis and the contralateral testis in confirmed torsion, and possible orchidectomy if the affected testis is non-viable. Fixation in a negative exploration depends on operative findings.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: If he is Gillick competent he consents, and I would explain to both of them, honestly, that the testis may need to be removed. If he lacked competence, his mother, with parental responsibility, could consent. Neither route should delay theatre.

failures.move: Delays exploration for ultrasound, blood tests or transfer when safe local surgery is available.
failures.consequence: Testicular viability is lost while waiting. This is a critical fail.

failures.move: Treats suspected torsion as infection because there is no fever.
Ignores the 15-year-old and takes consent from his mother alone.
failures.consequence: Fails to involve a young person who may be competent to consent.

knowledge.fact: If torsion cannot confidently be excluded, arrange immediate surgical assessment and emergency scrotal exploration; do not delay for ultrasound, blood tests or transfer when safe local surgery is available.
In confirmed torsion, fix a viable affected testis and the contralateral testis; fixation in a negative exploration depends on operative findings.
Adolescent torsion is usually intravaginal with a bell-clapper deformity; neonatal torsion is commonly extravaginal.
A young person under 16 who is competent can consent to treatment; involve parents with their agreement.

recall.think: A testis that is losing its blood supply.
recall.say: “Suspected torsion: I need immediate surgical assessment and theatre.”
do: Call the surgeon and theatre now
Nil by mouth, analgesia, IV access
Consent with the young person, involving his mother

numbers.meaning: no ultrasound or blood tests should delay exploration when torsion cannot be excluded

recall.trap: No fever, a normal blood test, or waiting for a scan.
recall.finish: Exploration, detorsion, fixation of both sides in confirmed torsion, orchidectomy if non-viable.

partner.opening: A 15-year-old presents with sudden severe unilateral scrotal pain and nausea. The affected testis is high-riding with a transverse lie. Explain the anatomy, immediate management and operative principles.
partner.actorBrief: If the candidate raises consent, the boy says: “Do I get a say, or does Mum decide?” His mother is supportive and wants to be involved.

push.question: What is the usual anatomical mechanism?
Would you get an ultrasound first?
push.expect: No: do not delay exploration for imaging.

push.question: He is 15. Who consents?
push.expect: Him, if Gillick competent, with his mother involved.

curveballs.safeAnswer: Absence of fever does not exclude torsion; the acute presentation and examination findings are more important.

curveballs.prompt: The children's hospital is an hour away. Should we transfer him?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Not if safe local surgery is available: explore without delay.
